tensions.name: Which judge bias to fight first: position or style
tensions.resolution: Style-first portfolio wins for this assignment: formatting normalization + anti-verbosity/format clauses + length-controlled analysis are mandatory; position-swap auditing stays as a verification harness (consistency ≥0.80) rather than the headline mitigation. Load-bearing reason: the only multi-family controlled measurement in the corpus ranks style bias an order of magnitude above position, and style is cheaper to neutralize deterministically than position is to average away.

side_a.evidence: 9 debias strategies × 5 judges × 4 bias types: style bias 0.10-0.76 baseline (mostly markdown-over-plain), position bias ≤0.04; mid-tier Gemini 2.5 Flash + Combined Budget reaches 71.0% agreement at ~$0.001/eval, 15× cheaper than frontier
side_a.position: Style bias dominates; position bias is second-order

side_b.evidence: GPT-4 flips ~35% of pairwise verdicts on order swap; IJCNLP 2025: 15 judges × 150k instances with systematic order-sensitivity; standard mitigation is dual-call swap averaging
side_b.position: Position bias is the headline threat; swap-averaging is the core mitigation

tensions.name: Caged judge vs human-only scoring for reply quality
tensions.resolution: Caged judge wins as headline instrument ONLY behind the tiered gates (human-human first, cross-family judge, swap/length/self-preference audits, disagreement analysis); RAGAS reference-free scores stay secondary diagnostics. Load-bearing reason: correlations up to .81 exist but are task-scoped, while bias mechanisms (self-preference structural, verbosity, style) are general — the cage is what transfers.

side_a.evidence: G-Eval Spearman .514; output-based judges Pearson .81/.68 on code tasks; calibrated longitudinal tau .59-.68; mid-tier + debias beats frontier at 15× lower cost
side_a.position: A rubric-pinned, mitigated, human-anchored LLM judge can headline reply-quality eval

side_b.evidence: Human-equivalent on only 4/11 criteria in global-health eval; GEMBA .09 on near-perfect MT; self-enhancement bias irreducible under swap debiasing (formal); reference-free scores test-time-optimizable and at times anti-human
side_b.position: Judges are systematically biased; bare judge scores prove nothing without human agreement

tensions.name: SetFit-first routing vs native-LLM classification
tensions.resolution: SetFit-first with MC-dropout routing wins as the default architecture (within ~2% F1 at ~50% latency cut and order-of-magnitude cost cut), with MaxProb + temperature as the mandatory baseline the router must beat on AURC. Load-bearing reason: the hybrid is the only option that simultaneously satisfies the accuracy bar, the latency/cost story, and the 15-minute reproducibility constraint.

side_a.evidence: Hybrid within ~2% of native LLM (0.737 vs 0.760 ex-shift) at ~50% reduced latency; SetFit 56× faster than best LLM; neg-aug +>5%; RAG-filtered dynamic few-shot $42 vs $740 per 3k queries
side_a.position: Small fine-tuned classifier first, LLM only on uncertain routes

side_b.evidence: GPT-3.5/4 in-context beats fine-tuned non-generative models on Banking77 with fewer examples; zero training, handles wording variance and <5/class regimes
side_b.position: Native LLM few-shot classifier wins on accuracy and robustness

tensions.name: Hybrid retrieval justified vs dense-only sufficiency
tensions.resolution: Hybrid wins by default on mechanism (pooling destroys lexical identity; inverted index preserves it) but the claim is gated: ≥5pt identifier-stratum Recall@10 on brand data, else revert to dense-plus-fallback. Load-bearing reason: dense silent failure (fluent, confident, wrong-specifics replies with no error firing) is the exact hallucination shape that kills trust, and Twitter support concentrates every dense-hostile feature.

side_a.evidence: Turion stack +30% over pure dense (+11-17pts recall); WANDS tuned hybrid +7.4%; Anthropic contextual −49-67% failure; BEIR cross-domain precedent; silent-failure mechanism agreed across 5 sources
side_a.position: BM25 + dense RRF + cross-encoder rerank over thread-window chunks is the default

side_b.evidence: Embedded single-store competitive at small scale with far less setup; naive RRF only +1.2% blended; two indices + rerank latency + fusion fragility are real ops costs
side_b.position: Pure dense suffices until hybrid proves its margin on brand data

tensions.name: Synthetic augmentation for rare intents: help or bleed
tensions.resolution: Real-first synthesis: tiny synthetic ablation only (≤+7 per intent), labeled ESTIMATED until golden-gated, because the bleed mechanism (generation into neighbor intents) is worst exactly where the submission needs help (close intents). Load-bearing reason: two independent Banking77 studies agree on the sweet spot and the failure mode; the corpus gives no Twitter-specific counter-evidence.

side_a.evidence: RAG-filtered dynamic demos beat full prompts cheaper AND better; cluster-77-into-10 + generate 20 helps to +5/+10 total; IntentBERT shows small real data suffices
side_a.position: LLM-generated training data fixes rare-intent starvation

side_b.evidence: GPT augmentation helps only for distinct intents; on close intents it generates neighbor-intent utterances (measured); past ~+7 synthetic per intent hurts; real always beats synthetic
side_b.position: Synthetic data cross-contaminates close intents and must be capped

tensions.name: Escalated handoff: show the draft or defer-only
tensions.resolution: Defer-only handoff wins (reason code + evidence, suppressed draft hidden unless requested). Load-bearing reason: the only human-factors evidence in the corpus is directional and high-stakes — showing low-confidence guesses degrades handler accuracy, which compounds the exact false-auto-handle risk escalation exists to prevent.

side_a.evidence: Informing humans of deferral status WITHOUT surfacing the uncertain guess improves downstream human accuracy; revealing the low-confidence guess degrades it (Bondi et al. 2021)
side_a.position: Defer-only: reason + evidence, draft hidden unless requested

side_b.evidence: Post-abstention re-attempting lifts coverage ~80% without accuracy loss; recovery-before-escalate converts abstention cost into measured wins; handler sees more context with draft visible
side_b.position: Show the draft with the escalation for handler efficiency
